title: XMATCH and XLOOKUP equate ligatures and combining sequences in exact mode, while wildcard ? counts UTF-16 units
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, XMATCH and XLOOKUP in default exact mode (match_mode 0) equate text by Excel's full collation rather than UTF-16 length: "e"&UNICHAR(769) matches precomposed "é", "ss"/"SS" matches "ß", "ae" matches "æ", and "a"&UNICHAR(173)&"b" matches "ab". By contrast, wildcard mode (match_mode 2) counts "?" in UTF-16 code units ("??" matches "😀", "?" skips to "a"). Unlike MATCH/VLOOKUP, blank lookup_value matches blank cells, and approximate searches order numbers < text < logicals < errors < blanks.
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in dczsn1_collation (rows 118-126) and fn1_collation (rows 218, 220), and matched across 3,373/3,373 XMATCH and 3,360/3,360 XLOOKUP full-bank rows.
